result.scope: Complete pinned original FileHasher body, real .NET SHA256 and owned filesystem; in-memory cache/log adapters, not original DB or Jellyfin runtime. Counterexamples asserted, not repaired.

native_control.adapters: Minimal in-memory keyed cache and no-op logger; original DB, scanner and Jellyfin not executed.

findings: Whole DuplicateScanner now read. Metadata grouping and edition splitting precede optional SHA256 check: this is not exhaustive arbitrary-file exact dedup. Books use ISBN/title; movies provider+year or normalized title/year/filename; audio provider or artist/album/title/truncated duration/filename.
NormalizeName removes all characters outside ASCII a-z0-9. Non-Latin filenames can collapse to empty normalization; no native scanner reproduction performed.
Hash match overrides title/runtime vetoes and scores exact confidence 1.0, but trusts FileHasher cached digest. No byte-by-byte comparison observed in these two whole bodies.

Full original FileHasher native controls: SHA256 baseline, restored-size/mtime stale hash, cancelled cache-hit returns cached digest, cancelled fresh hashing propagates cancellation. Four assertions pass; these preserve counterexamples, not fixes.
Existing rrrah fresh-byte exact confirmation and repeated-metadata tests address relevant identity boundary. No GPL implementation copied and no production change from this review.
Scanner considers positive-size non-symlink candidates first when ranking, reappending excluded candidates as losers. This is source policy only, not disposal qualification.
